name: Everest Base Camp
tagline: Lukla to the foot of the world's highest mountain.

cairns.title: Lukla
cairns.body: Nearly every Everest trek begins here, at an airstrip carved into a mountainside and pitched at an angle so aircraft slow down uphill. There is no road in. From this point onward, everything ahead — every load, every meal, every climber — arrives on foot, by yak, or by helicopter.

cairns.title: The Dudh Koshi
cairns.body: The river running beside the trail is glacial meltwater, pale with rock flour ground fine by ice — which is where its name, 'milk river', comes from. The trail crosses it repeatedly on steel suspension bridges strung high above the water, because the valley floor is too steep and too flood-prone to follow directly.

cairns.title: Himalayan Monal
cairns.body: A pheasant that looks implausible in flight: metallic green, copper and blue, with a thin crest like a lightning rod. Monals forage on steep hillsides, digging for roots and grubs with their beaks, and are most often seen at dawn between about 2,500 and 4,500 metres.

cairns.title: Namche Bazaar
cairns.body: A town built into a natural amphitheatre, and for centuries a trading post between Tibet and the lowlands. Almost everyone climbing higher stops here for two nights — not for comfort, but because the body needs time to make more red blood cells before going on.

cairns.title: Tengboche Monastery
cairns.body: The largest Buddhist monastery in the Khumbu, set on a ridge with Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam behind it. Expeditions have traditionally paused here to receive a blessing before continuing toward the mountain. The building was destroyed by fire in 1989 and rebuilt with help from the wider climbing community.

cairns.title: Thin Air
cairns.body: At Dingboche each breath carries roughly 60% of the oxygen available at sea level. Altitude sickness is not about fitness — strong walkers get it and cautious ones don't — which is why the rule on this trail is to gain height slowly and sleep lower than the highest point you reached that day.

cairns.title: Khumbu Glacier
cairns.body: From Lobuche the trail runs alongside a glacier several kilometres wide, buried under so much rubble that it looks like a grey moraine field. It is moving — slowly, constantly — and the sound of it shifting and cracking carries a long way in cold air.

cairns.title: Snow Leopard
cairns.body: Almost nobody sees one. They hunt blue sheep across broken ground above 3,000 metres, and their coats break up their outline so completely that researchers usually work from camera traps and tracks rather than sightings. Finding a single pugmark in fresh snow is considered a good day.

cairns.title: Everest Base Camp
cairns.body: Not a building or a viewpoint — a stretch of rubble-covered glacier that shifts under the tents each season, and from which the summit itself isn't even visible. In spring it becomes a temporary town of several hundred people. You have walked 62 kilometres and climbed 2,500 vertical metres to stand on moving ice.
